reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.020:11657 (subsections 1-4) and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 §§ 2 to 5, A.L. 1992 S.B. 676 adopted by referendum, Proposition C, November 3, 1992), and verified all fingerprints. Checked ex officio versus gubernatorially appointed membership, four-member party cap, six-member quorum and voting threshold, and per diem/expense entitlement limited to appointed members. Retained all four drafted headings.

headings.title: Creation of Missouri Housing Development Commission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 §§ 2–5, A.L. 1992 S.B. 676 adopted by Proposition C referendum, Nov. 3, 1992). Establishes the Missouri Housing Development Commission as a state governmental instrumentality and body corporate and politic.

headings.title: Commission membership, qualifications, terms, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (including 1992 Proposition C referendum adoption). Sets ex officio members (governor, lieutenant governor, state treasurer, attorney general) and six gubernatorially appointed members with senate advice and consent, housing/finance/construction knowledge, four-member political party cap, initial staggered and four-year terms, vacancy appointments, and reappointment eligibility.

headings.title: Quorum, effect of vacancies, and voting threshold
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Sets a six-member quorum, preserves quorum authority despite vacancies, and requires an affirmative vote of at least six members for commission action.

headings.title: Per diem compensation and expenses for appointed members
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Entitles gubernatorially appointed commission members (distinguished from ex officio members) to fifty dollars per diem plus reasonable and necessary expenses actually incurred under sections 215.010 to 215.250.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.030:47716 (subsections 1-3 including all 26 subdivisions of subsection 1) and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 § 6 through A.L. 2019 S.B. 17 merged with S.B. 185), and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 135.530 distressed-community housing authority, credit-rating standards, archived wording ("approve mortgagors" in (3), "project assistant services" in (8)), January 1, 1999 rulemaking repeal and section 536.028 nonseverability, and MOSERS eligibility under chapters 104 and 105. Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: General and enumerated powers of the commission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including all 26 subdivisions) and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 § 6 through A.L. 2019 S.B. 17 merged with S.B. 185). Grants necessary and appropriate powers including housing and section 135.530 distressed-community loans, loan insurance, construction and temporary loans, income definitions, fees, investments and rating standards, property transactions, bonds and notes, technical and consultative services, housing research, and weatherization loans/bonds; retains exact archived wording ('approve mortgagors' in (3), 'project assistant services' in (8)).

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance, 1999 repeal, and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires compliance with chapter 536 and section 536.028 after January 1, 1999, repeals pre-1999 rulemaking delegations while preserving earlier valid rules, and includes a section 536.028 nonseverability clause.

headings.title: Employee eligibility for state retirement system
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Makes all commission employees eligible for Missouri state employees' retirement system membership subject to applicable provisions of chapters 104 and 105.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.033:11659 (subsections 1-11 including all subdivisions and paragraphs) and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 566 § 12), and verified all fingerprints. Checked chapter 610 exemption, section-specific definitions, archived grammar in subsection 3 ("receives investments from investors and invest such funds"), compensated fund services, 16-member board composition and ex officio officials, staggered terms, expense-only service, fidelity bonds, MHDC funding, and February 15 annual report. Retained all eleven drafted headings.

headings.title: Missouri Equity Fund Support Corporation and chapter 610 exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 566 § 12). Authorizes the commission to create the Missouri Equity Fund Support Corporation to promote housing equity funds for low-income affordable housing, and declares it is not a political subdivision and not subject to chapter 610.

headings.title: Definitions for housing equity fund provisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(5)) and history note. Defines 'developer', 'housing equity fund', 'investors', 'nonprofit corporation', and 'tax credit development' for section 215.033.

headings.title: Establishing and operating housing equity funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the nonprofit corporation to establish and operate, or assist and advise in establishing and operating, the housing equity fund investing investor moneys in tax credit developments.

headings.title: Corporate powers and fee-based fund services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including subdivisions (1)–(5) and paragraphs (a)–(e)) and history note. Grants powers to contract for compensated legal, technical, administrative, marketing, and underwriting services to housing equity funds, sue and be sued, contract generally, acquire and dispose of property, and borrow at up to market interest rates.

headings.title: Board of directors composition and appointment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (including subdivisions (1)–(12)) and history note. Establishes a sixteen-member board appointed by the governor with housing knowledge: five sector representatives, five investor representatives (with fallback to subdivisions (1)–(5)), and six ex officio state officials.

headings.title: Appointed directors' terms and filling vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Sets four-year terms (and initial staggered two-, three-, and four-year terms) for non-ex-officio directors until successors are appointed, and fills unexpired-term vacancies in the original manner.

headings.title: Uncompensated board service and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Prohibits compensation for board service while permitting reimbursement of actual and necessary expenses incurred in performing duties.

headings.title: Board officers and corporation-paid fidelity bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Directs electing a chair and other officers and provides that any board-required officer bond has premiums borne by the nonprofit corporation.

headings.title: Personnel, compensation, quarters, and equipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Directs the board to employ necessary personnel, fix compensation, and provide suitable quarters and equipment to operate the housing equity fund.

headings.title: Commission start-up and operating funding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Authorizes the commission to provide start-up costs by grant or loan and subsequent operating funds as it determines.

headings.title: Annual report contents and February 15 submission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Requires publishing an annual report on fund establishment, operations, project types, and expenditures, submitted to the governor, general assembly, and commission on or before February 15.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.034:57135 (subsections 1-4) and all source notes (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 215.035, A.L. 2025 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 4; effective 6-14-25), and verified all fingerprints. Audited the June 14, 2025 disaster emergency-aid amendment (immediate transfer upon gubernatorial request for a presidential disaster declaration and permissive waiver of administrative burdens/costs), 2% administrative cost cap, annual commitment/expenditure of deposits and interest, and section 33.080 exemption. Revised subsection 1 title from "Missouri Housing Trust Fund creation, disaster transfers, and funding" to "Missouri Housing Trust Fund creation, funding, and disaster relief" to encompass both transfers and permissive waivers; retained subsections 2, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Missouri Housing Trust Fund creation, funding, and disaster relief
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section notes (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 215.035, A.L. 2025 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 4; effective 6-14-25). Establishes the fund, directs fiscal-year allocation to the commission, provides immediate transfer and permissive waivers of administrative burdens/costs (allocation plan, notice of funding availability, public hearings) for emergency-aid appropriations upon a gubernatorial request for a presidential disaster declaration, lists funding sources including section 59.319 user fees, and limits uses to sections 215.034 to 215.039. Revised title to "disaster relief" to cover both immediate transfers and administrative waivers added in 2025.

headings.title: Two-percent cap on commission administrative costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes (effective 6-14-25). Pays commission program administrative costs from the fund, capped annually at two percent of net annual revenues received into the fund.

headings.title: Annual commitment or expenditure of deposits and interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes (effective 6-14-25). Requires the commission to commit or expend annually deposited money and all earned interest solely for purposes established in sections 215.034 to 215.039.

headings.title: Exemption from biennial transfer to general revenue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes (effective 6-14-25). Exempts unexpended fund balances at the end of a biennium year from transfer to general revenue under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.036:57136 (subsections 1-5 including both 1-to-8-person percentage tables and the continuation paragraph after the subsection 2 table) and all source notes (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 215.036 subsecs. 1 to 4, A.L. 2025 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 4; effective 6-14-25), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed subsection 2 title covers both the 35%-66% schedule and the continuation paragraph defining "geographical area" for the entire section, subsection 3 distinguishes the 18%-33% priority schedule, subsection 4 retains archived spelling "dispersed" in notes, and subsection 5 accurately reflects the June 14, 2025 natural disaster exemption from subsections 2-4 and 75% median-income cap. Retained all five drafted headings.

headings.title: Eligible housing uses and fifty-percent biennial allocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section notes (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 215.036 subsecs. 1–4, A.L. 2025 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 4; effective 6-14-25). Directs using trust fund moneys for loans or grants assisting households at or below subsection 2 and 3 income limits, with at least fifty percent over each section 33.080 biennium awarded for subsection 3 income levels.

headings.title: Household income limits and geographical area definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including the 1-to-8-person percentage table from 35% to 66% and the continuation paragraph) and section notes (effective 6-14-25). Establishes the upper income eligibility schedule and defines 'geographical area' for the section using HUD Section 8 fair-market-rent areas or state median family income, whichever is larger.

headings.title: Lower household income limits for priority allocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including the 1-to-8-person percentage table from 18% to 33%) and section notes (effective 6-14-25). Establishes the lower income eligibility schedule referenced by the fifty-percent biennial allocation in subsection 1.

headings.title: Thirty-percent biennial allocation to not-for-profit housing providers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes (effective 6-14-25). Requires allocating at least thirty percent of funds ('dispersed' in archived text) during each two-year period to not-for-profit housing providers under chapter 355 or IRC section 42(h)(5)(C).

headings.title: Natural disaster emergency aid exemption and income cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and section notes (effective 6-14-25). Exempts disaster emergency aid appropriations from subsections 2 to 4 when the governor requests a presidential disaster declaration, setting eligibility at or below 75% of area or state median family income, whichever is greater.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.037:11662 (subsections 1-3) and history note (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 215.036 subsecs. 5, 6, 7), and verified all fingerprints. Checked 30% gross rent cap, 18-year/loan-length/longer-period duration, non-telephone utility allowance, title covenant requirement, and clear distinction between subsection 2 (rental-rate certification/audits) and subsection 3 (tenant income-eligibility certification/audits). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Maximum gross rental rates, utility allowances, and title covenants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 215.036 subsecs. 5, 6, 7). Caps gross rent at 30% of maximum eligible household income for 18 years, the loan length, or a longer commission-imposed period for projects assisted under sections 215.036 to 215.038, includes non-telephone utilities with utility-allowance reductions when tenant-paid, and requires incorporating a legal covenant in property title.

headings.title: Annual owner certification and audits of rental rates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 3 by requiring annual owner certification of rental-rate compliance under sections 215.036 to 215.038, with commission forms and discretionary audits.

headings.title: Annual owner certification and audits of tenant income eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 by requiring annual owner certification that all tenants in assisted projects are income eligible under sections 215.036 to 215.038, with commission forms and discretionary audits.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.039:11664 (subsections 1-3) and history note (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 215.038), and verified all fingerprints. Checked discretionary municipal/county agreements, administrative and section 215.030/chapter 536 rulemaking powers, and January 15 annual housing trust fund report. Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Agreements with municipal or county government entities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 215.038). Authorizes the commission in its discretion to enter into agreements assisting municipal or county programs that meet Missouri housing trust fund purposes under sections 215.034 to 215.039.

headings.title: Administrative powers and rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Grants all powers necessary to carry out sections 215.034 to 215.039, including rulemaking authority pursuant to section 215.030 and chapter 536.

headings.title: Annual housing trust fund report and January 15 deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires publishing an annual report on assisted project types and fund expenditures and submitting copies to the governor and general assembly on or before January 15.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.054:11667 (subsections 1-7 including subdivisions (1)-(5) of subsection 3) and history note (L. 1993 S.B. 388, A.L. 1994 S.B. 742), and verified all fingerprints. Explicitly checked subsection 3(5) (non-parallel sentence under the fund-interest lead-in dedicating 50% of habilitation center sale proceeds, subject to appropriations, to habilitation center construction or substantial renovation), joint DMH/MHDC project selection and catchment-area investment, section 33.080 exemption qualified by "except by appropriation", and St. Joseph State Hospital carve-out. Revised subsection 7 title from "Exclusion of St. Joseph State Hospital sale proceeds" to "Exclusion and use of St. Joseph State Hospital proceeds" to capture the mandated construction use; retained subsections 1 through 6.

headings.title: Creation and administration of Mental Health Housing Trust Fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 S.B. 388, A.L. 1994 S.B. 742). Creates the Mental Health Housing Trust Fund in the state treasury to be administered by the commission in cooperation with the department of mental health.

headings.title: Deposits of surplus property proceeds and state treasurer investment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs proceeds from selling surplus former department of mental health real property into the fund upon appropriation, with state treasurer investment and annual interest crediting to the fund.

headings.title: Authorized uses of fund interest and habilitation center proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)-(5)) and history note. Lists permitted uses of fund interest upon appropriation in subdivisions (1)-(4) (community housing grants/loans, vouchers, home-ownership programs, matching grants), and in structurally non-parallel subdivision (5) allocates 50% of proceeds from the sale of habilitation center property, subject to appropriations, to constructing or substantially renovating habilitation centers; heading accurately distinguishes both interest uses and habilitation sale proceeds.

headings.title: Project selection, financial review, priority, and geographic investment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers joint project selection, commission financial feasibility review, funding department-approved feasible projects in department priority order, and investing surplus property proceeds in facility catchment municipalities and other high-need municipalities.

headings.title: Commission fund management and reporting duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs commission management of the fund, including accepting deposits, reviewing and funding department-approved projects, and reporting fund activities to the department of mental health.

headings.title: Exemption from biennial transfer except by appropriation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Exempts fund moneys from transfer to general revenue at the end of the biennium under section 33.080, except by appropriation.

headings.title: Exclusion and use of St. Joseph State Hospital proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Excepts St. Joseph State Hospital real property sale proceeds from subsection 2 trust fund deposits and directs that they be used to construct the new state hospital in St. Joseph, Missouri. Revised title to reflect both the exclusion from the fund and the mandated construction use.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.060:11668 (subsections 1-5) and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 §§ 10, 11 through A.L. 1993 H.B. 566), and verified all fingerprints. Checked interim/permanent loans and ancillary facilities, rental/cooperative/condominium project loans, dwelling weatherization loans, small owner-occupied and 1/4-mile rental property loan program, and DNR-consulted weatherization standards for section 215.030 dwellings. Retained all five drafted headings.

headings.title: Interim and permanent housing mortgage loans and ancillary facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 §§ 10, 11 through A.L. 1993 H.B. 566). Authorizes interim and permanent mortgage loans for construction and rehabilitation of needed low- and moderate-income residential housing, including regulation-permitted ancillary commercial and appurtenant facilities.

headings.title: Loans for rental, cooperative, or condominium housing projects
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes commission loans to approved mortgagors to develop and operate residential housing projects under sections 215.010 to 215.250 on a rental, cooperative, or condominium basis.

headings.title: Low-interest loans for dwelling weatherization
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes making or purchasing low-interest loans to approved mortgagors for weatherization of single-family and multifamily dwellings.

headings.title: Loan program for small owner-occupied and nearby rental properties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs establishing a loan program for approved mortgagors to purchase and develop owner-occupied multiunit dwellings of up to four units and other residential rental property within one-fourth mile of the owner's residence.

headings.title: Weatherization standards for dwellings built under section 215.030
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires single-family and multifamily dwellings constructed under section 215.030 to follow weatherization standards set by the commission in consultation with the department of natural resources.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.120:11675 (subsections 1-4) and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 §§ 17 to 20), and verified all fingerprints. Checked negotiable revenue bond/note issuance under sections 215.010 to 215.250, renewal notes and refunding bonds, 20-year note and 50-year bond maturity caps and public/private sale terms, and state nonliability with required face statement. Retained all four drafted headings.

headings.title: Issuance of negotiable revenue bonds and notes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 §§ 17–20). Authorizes issuing negotiable revenue bonds or notes for commission corporate purposes under sections 215.010 to 215.250, including housing mortgage loans, rehabilitation, construction, reserves, and incidental expenditures.

headings.title: Renewal notes, refunding bonds, and use of proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes renewal notes, bonds to pay notes, refunding bonds (for matured or unmatured bonds, alone or combined with other purposes), and applying proceeds to purchase, redeem, or pay refunded bonds.

headings.title: Authorizing resolutions, maturity limits, terms, and sale
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires commission resolution authorizing notes and bonds under sections 215.010 to 215.250, caps maturities at 20 years for notes/renewals and 50 years for bonds, covers interest/form/execution/redemption terms, and permits public or private sale.

headings.title: State nonliability and required face statement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Declares that commission notes and bonds are not a debt or liability of the state and must carry a statement to that effect on their face.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.170:11680 (subsections 1-3 including subdivisions (1)-(5) of subsection 2) and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 §§ 25, 26, 27), and verified all fingerprints. Checked 30-day payment default and statutory/agreement default triggers, 25% holder threshold for trustee appointment and mandatory action, sections 215.170-215.190 scope, acceleration and annulment conditions, and incidental trustee powers. Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Default triggers and holder appointment of a trustee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 H.B. 130 §§ 25–27). Permits holders of 25% in aggregate principal amount of an issue to appoint a trustee upon a 30-day payment default, statutory noncompliance under sections 215.010 to 215.250, or agreement default, for purposes of sections 215.170, 215.180, and 215.190.

headings.title: Trustee enforcement, accounting, injunction, and acceleration powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(5)) and history note. Specifies actions the trustee may take—and must take upon written request of 25% of holders—including enforcing rights and fee/payment collection, suing on notes or bonds, requiring trust accounting, enjoining violations, and accelerating maturity or annulling acceleration with 25% holder consent after cure.

headings.title: Incidental trustee powers to represent holders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants the trustee additional powers necessary or appropriate to exercise specified functions or generally represent bondholders and noteholders in enforcing and protecting their rights.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.263:11692 (subsections 1-2) and all source notes (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 1 subsecs. 3, 4, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1965; effective 4-01-11, see § 135.204; Revisor footnote stating section 215.261 was repealed by S.B. 58, 2015), and verified all fingerprints. Retained exact archived cross-reference range "sections 215.261 to 215.263" in subsection 1 without altering the source reference or overstating current operability, and kept subsection 2 neutral regarding "the commission" given the 2015 repeal of section 215.261. Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Definition of affordable housing for sections 215.261 to 215.263
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section notes (L. 1994 H.B. 1745 § 1 subsecs. 3, 4, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1965; effective 4-01-11, see § 135.204; footnote noting section 215.261 was repealed by S.B. 58, 2015). Defines 'affordable housing' for archived range sections 215.261 to 215.263 using 115% county median income from specified five-year American Community Survey estimates and 29% annual gross income affordability.

headings.title: Support staff provided by department of economic development
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes (effective 4-01-11 per § 135.204; footnote noting section 215.261 was repealed by S.B. 58, 2015). Directs the Missouri department of economic development to provide clerical, research, and general administrative support staff for "the commission" (retaining archived phrasing neutrally without speculating on the effect of the 2015 repeal of section 215.261).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.309:11696 (subsections 1-4 including subdivisions (1)-(9) of subsection 1 and subdivisions (1)-(6) of subsection 3) and all source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 378 § 20; Revisor footnote noting word "the" does not appear in original rolls at subsection 1(9)), and verified all fingerprints. Checked historical December 31, 1989 report deadline, FOIA exception in subsection 1(8), archived lead-in phrasing in subsection 3, and Title II Housing and Community Development Act of 1987 prepayment/plan disclosures in subsection 4. Retained all four drafted headings.

headings.title: Review of public records and 1989 subsidized housing report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(9)) and section notes (L. 1989 H.B. 378 § 20; Revisor footnote noting word 'the' does not appear in original rolls at subdivision (9)). Directs the commission to review HUD, state, and local records and produce a report on subsidized multifamily rental housing projects by December 31, 1989 with nine enumerated items (including a FOIA exception in (8)).

headings.title: Public availability of the subsidized housing report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Requires that the subsidized multifamily rental housing report be made available to the public.

headings.title: Distribution to project owners and required tenant disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)-(6)) and section notes. Requires the administering agency to distribute report copies to owners of subsidized multifamily rental housing projects (retaining archived lead-in wording "the following subsidized multifamily rental housing projects" before enumerating six information items) and requires those owners to provide the six listed ownership, management, mortgagee, and subsidy-termination items to current and new tenants.

headings.title: Disclosing federal prepayment notices and plans of action
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes. Requires state and local agencies receiving prepayment notices, plans of action, and other Title II federal Housing and Community Development Act of 1987 information to provide it to property tenants and their representatives and make it available to the public.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.311:11697 (subsections 1-5 including subdivisions (1)-(3) of subsection 2 and subdivisions (1)-(4) of subsection 5) and history note (L. 1989 H.B. 378 § 21), and verified all fingerprints. Checked subsidy request and notice-of-intent guidance under sections 215.300 to 215.318, affordability plan contents, owner revision authority, section 215.314 agreement criteria, and permissive incentives under sections 32.115 and 215.050. Retained all five drafted headings.

headings.title: Subsidy requests, commission guidance, and affordability plan submission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1989 H.B. 378 § 21). Covers owner requests for additional subsidies, commission provision of information on sections 215.300 to 215.318 incentives and affordability restrictions upon receiving a notice of intent, and owner submission of a plan to expand affordability.

headings.title: Required contents of a plan to expand affordability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history note. Requires the plan to describe requested state or local incentives after agency consultation, assess effects on present and future tenants (including affordability and maintenance), and include other commission-determined information.

headings.title: Revising and amending plans of action for approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits the owner to revise and amend the plan of action from time to time as necessary to obtain approval under this section.

headings.title: Commission agreements to satisfy section 215.314 criteria
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes the commission, after receiving a plan of action, to enter into agreements necessary to satisfy approval criteria under section 215.314.

headings.title: State and local incentives authorized in subsidy agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (including subdivisions (1)–(4)) and history note. Lists incentives that agreements may include if deemed necessary by the commission: section 32.115 state income tax credits, local property tax abatement recommendations, and section 215.050 second-mortgage financing and grants.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 215.318:11700 (subsections 1-2) and history note (L. 1989 H.B. 378 §§ 24, 25), and verified all fingerprints. Checked preemption of overlapping municipal or county ordinances by additional-subsidy agreements and voluntary owner-participation rule across sections 215.300 to 215.318. Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Subsidy agreements superseding local ordinances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1989 H.B. 378 §§ 24, 25). Provides that provisions of any agreement granting additional subsidies to an owner supersede municipal or county ordinances covering the same subject matter.

headings.title: Voluntary participation by property owners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Clarifies that nothing in sections 215.300 to 215.318 requires an owner to enter into referred agreements or accept subsidies.
